newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNI FOCUS -- prices steady, NYC deal priced.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNI FOCUS -- prices steady, NYC deal priced.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were largely unchanged in early trade as Lehman Brothers tentatively priced $739 million New York City general obligation bonds at a top yield of 6.0 percent in 2016.
"I think it's going to do well, I really do," one trader said, adding that the City has expanded its appeal to a broader buyer base.
City paper has performed "remarkably well" over the last year and a half to two years, the trader said.
"I think people have a different perception of the city than they did before," he said.
Back in the secondary market, muni prices were steady but quiet as players took a wait-and-see stance.

"I think they want to get a feel for how it's all going to play out," the trader said. "We've been outperforming (Treasuries) for a while. I think we are technically in very good shape, and I think that's what's held our bidside in fairly well."

Wednesday's actively quoted issues included Broward County, Fla., Professional Sports Facilities tax revenue bonds of September 2028. The 5-5/8 percent bonds had a 5.72 percent net bid, an improvement from Tuesday's closing net bid of 5.74 percent.

In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was down 10/32 at 96-6/32 to yield 6.93 percent. In debt futures, the June municipal contract was up 2/32 at 116-24/32. The June T-bond contract was down 2/32 at 109-25/32. The MOB spread was 223 ticks.
Also in Wednesday's new issue action, AG Edwards & Sons tentatively priced $139 million Cleveland Stadium, Ohio, certificates of participation at a top yield of 5.70 percent in 2027.
